assumptions: Assumes the dataset is not fully anonymized and retains granular location and health attributes.

title: Cloud-hosting metadata can create attributable evidence about individuals and processing
description: Hosting and replication at the third-party cloud provider can generate metadata such as storage logs, replication events, timestamps, tenant identifiers, and access records that may be attributable to specific individuals or records, undermining deniability about the presence or handling of their data.
assumptions: Assumes provider-side operational metadata is retained and can be associated with specific datasets or data subjects.
uncertainty_note: The exact granularity of provider metadata is not specified in the flow description.

title: Cloud provider can detect sensitive hosting and replication activity
description: Because analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset are hosted and replicated at the cloud provider, the provider can observe the existence, timing, scale, and patterns of these communications and storage operations, revealing sensitive processing activity.
assumptions: Assumes the third-party provider has operational visibility into hosted assets and replication traffic/operations.

title: Propagation of full dataset to third-party cloud provider may exceed necessity
description: The flow propagates analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset to a third-party cloud hosting provider for hosting and replication. Sharing the full dataset with an external party may exceed what is strictly necessary for the analytics function, increasing disclosure exposure.
assumptions: Assumes not all hosted data elements are strictly required by the cloud provider to deliver the intended service.
uncertainty_note: Necessity depends on architectural and contractual constraints not provided in the prompt.

title: Third-party cloud hosting exposes personal data to an additional predetermined party
description: By hosting and replicating the full health and location dataset at the cloud provider, personal data becomes accessible to an additional predetermined external party beyond the analytics service itself, increasing exposure of highly sensitive information.
assumptions: Assumes the provider can access or otherwise process the hosted data at least at an administrative or service-operation level.

title: Data subjects may be unaware their full health and location data is hosted and replicated by a cloud provider
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their full health and location dataset, as well as derived analytics assets, are stored and replicated at a third-party cloud provider, limiting transparency about downstream storage and disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes this third-party hosting and replication arrangement is not clearly disclosed to data subjects.
uncertainty_note: The prompt does not specify what privacy notices or disclosures are provided.

title: Third-party replication can hinder erasure or rectification across copies
description: Replication of the full health and location dataset at the cloud provider can make it harder for data subjects to ensure their data is corrected or deleted across all hosted and replicated copies, reducing intervenability.
assumptions: Assumes multiple copies, backups, or replicas are maintained by the provider and are not instantly synchronized with rectification/erasure requests.
uncertainty_note: Specific deletion and synchronization capabilities are not described in the flow context.

title: Transferring the full health and location dataset to cloud hosting may violate data minimization
description: Sending the full health and location dataset, along with analytics data and models, to a third-party cloud provider may involve processing more personal data than is necessary for the hosting purpose, creating a data-minimization compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes a reduced or de-identified dataset could have satisfied the hosting objective.
uncertainty_note: Whether minimization is violated depends on the precise hosting requirements and safeguards, which are not specified.

title: Cloud replication may create storage-limitation compliance risk
description: Replication of the full health and location dataset at the cloud provider increases the risk that personal data is retained in active replicas, backups, or recovery copies longer than functionally necessary, creating storage-limitation concerns.
assumptions: Assumes replicated copies and backups have retention periods that may outlast functional need.
uncertainty_note: Actual retention schedules and deletion guarantees are not provided.
